topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_01:
I never quite believed the rumors swirling about this place. Too much talk, not enough empirical evidence. And I know how far from truth rumors can be.

But now that I'm here, I'm forced to face the facts. There is something to the tales about the power located here that is true. 

These Upyr have access to magics I haven't seen before, and I have seen many. 

Is it because their archives hold ancient secrets? I have not been to one yet, so I cannot say for sure, but they have promised me the privilege, once I have accepted their ways. 

The temptation is strong. Perhaps I will finally find a way to cure the Lost here.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_02:
Curses, bah, that's not what is affecting me. 

That third-rate forture teller is as far from the truth as we are from my brother's workshop in Edengrove. 

These changes, they are part of the process which will bring me greater power. Though I admit, I had not realized they would be quite this painful. If only Britmar could see me know, what would she say?

Probably that it's a taste of my own medicine for what happened in Weaver's Fen. And she wouldn't be wrong.

Soon, they tell me, the pain will stop. Soon I will feel stronger. 

Soon.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_03:
My dearest Lilith, how can this be? How can one such as you be gone? You were supposed to be endless, like the sun, and without you my world has descended into endless night.

I do not know what to do without you by my side. How can I raise our daughter without your laughter, your smiles? I...

(tears mar the next few lines.)

There are rumors... whispers I have heard in shadowed places from people I would not have trusted in the past. They say there may be a way to return you to yourself. A relic, something from your past, my love. Something called the Tear of Gaea. It may not exist, but I shall find out. Nothing will stop me from discovering the truth.

For I will bring you back. If it is the last thing I do.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_04:
Have you heard that delectable sorceress has fallen for Dracula's promise? She's going to go through with it! 

Isn't that absolutely delicious! If I wasn't already undead, I would just die!

I can't wait to see what it's like to have her magics merged with ours! Can you imagine how that would taste? 

I haven't sampled something new in ages! 

And can you believe that those fools thought she's be at Bathory! Truly, toying with humans is such a delightful passtime. I shall never be bored of playing with my food.



Forever your friend, 

Z.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_05:
I've got more details that you'll just gobble up.

She didn't just fall for the promise, she agreed to be a thrall!

To think, agreeing to that! And the transformation has already begun! She's been trying to hold it back, the poor thing, and of course she's been unsuccessful. Good thing she's holed up in Memora Singur so that no one can stop her inevitable transformation. 

Just goes to show that magic does not make someone smarter. 



Your friend in the shadows, 

C.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_06:
Above the Door to Wisdom sits the Keystone of Knowledge. Held in place by Truth, needing no False Beliefs as mortar.

It guides the way to the Archives. A place where Wisdom thrives and Knowledges grows. 

An Oasis of Learning in a Desert of Ignorance.

Beware those who would turn the Keystone to their own Purposes, to Bar the Way.

Knowledge is meant to be Shared.

Those who would hoard Knowledge are Hiding more than the Truth. They are lying to themselves.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_07:
Here lies Apkulla, long may he teach. He was the last of the great Archivists, who oversaw the completion of the grand House Dracul, built to protect his beloved Archive. 


May his wisdom guide him through the great unknown.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_08:
Alecksi, my love, what a marvelous Archive! The history that fills this place is so rich, so vast. It's marvelous! Thank you for bringing me here.

Look at this! You have references about the location of the Tear of Gaea. 

Did you know it can only be activated with the blood of the Amara? It's a good thing there are no other Amara in this place. I wouldn't want to see this activated. 

No, I'm not going to find it and activate it! Darling, it may look like a simple jewel, but looks can be deceiving. Do you have any idea what will happen when it's used?

The power it requires... it's too much for the world. The cost it extracts is too high. It's call the Tear for good reason.

No, dear, it won't kill the user. It's much worse than that. It rips a hole in the very fabric of reality.

What comes through the hole, that's what you have to worry about. Because the Tear won't help you against that.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_01_09:
Oh look Alecksi! I didn't think I'd find this here.

It's the Amulet of Ninsun! It allows that which is physical to enter the nebulous realm of dreams. To cross the boundaries between the waking and the twilight world as simply as one would walk from the inside of a house to the outside.

My ancestors must have placed it here in the Archives, for protection. 

After all, it would be far too easy for someone to misuse a gift from Ninsun herself, when she walked through Aeternum. 

I'm glad that you are the one protecting it now.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_02_01:
We were there when you first found Thorpe in the forsaken grove after dragging yourself across a foreign beach.
We were there when you found your first settlement, and explored its charm and denizens.
We were there when you fought pirates, tigers, corrupted, ghosts, and all manner of hazards across the land.
We were there when you set foot on forsaken sands filled with lost secrets and hidden dangers.
We were there when you discovered the untamed wilds filled with beasts and verdant jungles.
We were there when you crept into the dark heart of lands filled with opulence, madness, and terror.

Through it all we watched. We delighted. We reveled in your enjoyment of every perfect moment, every carefully crafted story, and we even bore witness to the joining of two souls who met here in Aeternum.

We did it all for you dear adventurer.

Thank you for so many amazing stories, triumphs, and fits of laughter.

We raise a glass to our fallen comrades:

Divya
Shaun
Kelvin
Aaron

Good luck, and good night.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_01: There was a deliberate voluptuousness which was both thrilling and repulsive... I felt in my heart a wicked, burning desire that they would kiss me with those red lips. It is not good to note this down, lest someday it should meet Sarah’s eyes; and cause her pain. But it is the truth. They whispered together, and then they all three laughed—such a silvery, musical laugh, but as hard as though the sound never could have come through the softness of human lips.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_02: Sometimes, after an hour of apathy, my strange and beautiful companion would take my hand and hold it with a fond pressure... murmuring with a sigh, ‘You are mine, you shall be mine, and you and I are one forever.’ Then she would tremble and her lips in soft kisses gently glow upon my cheek.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_03: He seemed to lose all respect for what others deemed sacred; and there was something so singular in his conduct that, although he might sometimes attract the attention of the young and the thoughtless, he never engaged the affections of the virtuous and the wise.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_04: I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed. Everywhere I see bliss, from which I alone am irrevocably excluded. I was benevolent and good—misery made me a fiend. Make me happy, and I shall again be virtuous.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_05: It was Tildew, after all, and Tildew alone, that was guilty. Farragut was no more than a house for him... and yet the situation was one of appalling strangeness. For as the two natures that contended in the field of my consciousness... I was radically both.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_06: The fields once green now bear no wheat, only men that walk though slain. Each body keepeth its wound as a farmer his plough, yet onward they go, bound by unseen chains. No cry doth they utter, nor curse, nor groan—only the sound of feet upon earth that shall not rest. When night falleth they turn toward the living, as if called by some harvest yet unfinished.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_07: I opened the book at random and began to read. I had not read ten minutes before I felt vaguely uneasy. Then, by degrees, a sense of terror and dread grew upon me. I tried to shake it off, but I could not. My teeth were chattering, my hair was stiff, and my blood seemed to freeze.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_08: A sudden memory of the Thrall-things—the awful, white, half-human monsters—stole into my mind. Do they also come from that tremendous arena? I wondered... the shadows moved—a vast sea of shadows—unstirred by any wind. And I knew that they watched me.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_09: It was not a woman’s face. The semblance of a woman was there, the fair hair, the oval cheeks, the red lips; but all seemed to melt and shimmer before the eyes, and there was a look in the eyes that was not human, and the voice was faint and dull as the murmuring of the woods at night.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_10: There are forces close here that could kill a man outright, leave him neither wounded nor marked. I mean that some accident might happen to us. The spirit of the place is hostile. There’s something here that intends us harm. It is not the river, nor the forest, but something in the reeds.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_11: There was a figure in the bed. The head was invisible—there was a mass of crumpled linen—its arms lay upon the outside of the bedclothes. Then a shaking began—a straining, a heaving, as of something forced to raise itself. The room was full of it—the air thick with terror.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_12: Just at this moment, the shadowy object of alarm put itself in motion... and galloped away with him as fast as the horse could go. As they dashed through the hollow, the goblin rider suddenly turned and hurled his head at Artemis. It encountered his cranium with a tremendous crash—he tumbled headlong into the dust.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_13: Who is this invisible being that rules me, this unknowable creature, this wanderer from a world beyond ours? He haunts me, he is within me, he dominates me. I am lost! Someone possesses my soul and governs all my acts. I do not know what I do—he does it! My God! My God! Deliver me!
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_14: It is impossible to say how first the idea entered my brain; but once conceived, it haunted me day and night. Object there was none. Passion there was none. I loved the old man... I think it was his eye! Yes, it was this! One of his eyes resembled that of a vulture—a pale blue eye, with a film over it.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_15: Then suddenly I saw it. With only a slight churning to mark its rise to the surface, the thing slid into view above the dark waters. Vast, polyphemous, and loathsome, it darted like a stupendous monster of nightmares to the monolith. I think I went mad then.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_16: And they came to the great open doorway that ‘hath been open since the Beginning,’ and through which the cold steadfast light and the inscrutable silence of Evil ‘hath made for ever a silence that may be felt in all the Land.’ … And here will I tell how that the strange Quiet which did fill all the Land, seeming to brood within the night, was horrid beyond all the roarings … so that it had given my spirit some rest and assurance to hear but the far‑echoing, low thunder of the Great Laughter … Or the Baying of the Hounds, or the Roaring of the Giants, or any of those dreadful sounds … For they could not have offended me as did that time of silence; and so shall you judge how dreadful was that quiet, which did hold so much of horror.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_17: In the stillness of night she crept beside me, her face pale as a shroud, her eyes like coals banked in ash. She murmured, “Think not of freedom, for thy soul is chained to mine, as corpse to coffin.” At these words her hand grew colder than winter’s grave, and trembling seized her frame. With lips that reeked of earth newly broken, she kissed me, and I felt the long hunger of the dead.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_18: After I had breakfasted with Montgomery … we heard a rabbit squealing. … we stopped … and presently … he told me they were creatures made of the offspring of the Beast People … Before it could extricate itself we managed to catch it. It spat like a cat, scratched and kicked … It seemed to me rather a pretty little creature … I would imagine it might prove a convenient substitute for the common rabbit.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_19: Jennings spoke with the careful precision of a man accustomed to scientific observation, yet beneath his composed tone I detected lurking horror. He said: ‘I noticed first a small, twitching movement in the reflection of the glass opposite my dressing table. It seemed as though a monkey peered at me between the plates of glass. I shook my head, half in wonder, half in alarm. Yet when morning came, the reflection vanished—but not the dread I carried with me.’ He then described how each night the creature returned: sometimes as a pale, staring face; sometimes as the faint curl of a tail on the mirror’s edge. Hesselius writes to a colleague: “The form remains invisible to all except Jennings; and with each appearance its mockery deepens, its malignity becoming nearly tangible. He sleeps little, eats less, and is haunted—haunted beyond the power of reason to explain.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_04_20: At the ruined chapel they sit in rows, pale as wax and patient as stone. None dare name them living, though their eyes are ever open. It is told they wait the toll of a bell never forged, to rise as one and take back the world of breath. I did once draw near, and swear to God their lips moved, whispering prayers twisted into hungers no saint would claim.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_01: The hounds are responding well to the conditioning. They haven't barked or so much as whimpered at the new recruits, or any visiting Justicars. Unfortunately, one of them won't stop staring at the shadows in the corner of my tent…
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_02: I've been distracted by the hounds lately. They've been very obedient, and we've takent them on a few hunts for the beasts of this land, but in the night when I look at them it almost sounds like they are whispering to me.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_03: The hounds have been remarkably effective of late. Unfortunately they're a little too effective. We've not had a prisoner to interrogate for weeks. The hounds just rip them to shreds. I could have sworn I saw one's eyes glow with a bloodlust that I've never seen before.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_04: It's all become clear to me now. These creatures my hounds are becoming are the perfect tool to cleanse this land from the threat of the foul beasts that roam these forests.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_05: Whispers from the marrow now. Subject still screams when exposed to relics, but the screaming has begun to harmonize. Curious. I believe the bones are learning. I will need another priest. Preferably a young one.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_06: Subject retained partial lucidity post-severance. Attempted speech before its teeth folded inward. The language it used... I dream in it now. I will need more ink. And salt. Everything smells like fur.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_07: Subject expired during vivisection, yet continued to blink for twelve minutes. The eye looked beyond me. I am confident the soul remained inside the flesh. Next time I will not ask it questions, I will listen.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_08: The ghosts don’t scream like the others. They sing. I caught one in the mirror today. It looked like me. It asked me what I wanted, and I could not remember. I must remember. I will cut memory from brain if needed.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_09: Prisoner 33 still bites when fed. No longer bound by iron, just courtesy. Her teeth grow back faster each time. I stopped logging the escapes. If she wants out, she waits until I sleep. I’ve begun locking myself in.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_10: Captain says the new ones are spies. I say they don’t have enough eyes to be spies. Nothing on this isle does. Still, they writhe too much. I put them in the stone cells. Stone does not lie. Not yet.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_11: Traps 7 through 11 failed. Not from rust, but from decision. Steel no longer cuts when it's afraid. I laid blood across the thresholds instead. Something laughed from the tree line. It wasn’t cruel. It was amused.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_12: The beasts no longer move when we hunt. They wait. Patient, like saints before a sermon. I followed tracks that led to my own tent. My boots were still warm.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_13:
This new world, this new land, is rotten. The people here are heretical and mad. I am bound by my oaths to bring this land - and its people - back to the light. I shall perform rites of purification in Tularest. There, the jailers shall bring criminals, fathers will bring their daughters who have become too loose in their morals, mothers will bring their babes who are whelps of rebellion and are not responding to the belt.

Their souls will be cleansed.

Should they return to their wicked ways, I will need to be more creative.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_14:
Perhaps my heart has begun to harden. The weight of my purpose as a righteous enforcer of justice has begun to tip the scales.

I have dedicated my life to dispensing justice and have found that the answer is not always clear. I have found myself being deceitful, greedy, and prideful.

What is this moral decay I am afflicted with?

My mind burns, as if the light is scorching at the darkness there, as it aims to cleanse what is plaguing me. The light will prevail. I must persist through the pain. It is my punishment for my deviation.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_15: This darkness - this decay of my soul I am afraid has gotten too large for me to pray to the light alone. The eyes are the lamp of the body. Are they truly the windows to the soul? I cannot allow this darkness to spread. Others must not know the darkness that has seeped its way into my core. I feared I was at risk for excommunication, should I be found out. I sought guidance from other children of the light. I confessed my wrongdoings and how I have strayed from the church. It was then in which I discovered that the Inquisition itself is corrupt. This corruption is rooted far deeper than I ever could have imagined. I will not bear witness to this any longer. I will raze my soul from the inside out, beginning with my eyes.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_16:
I can still see it, this light that is darkness. It is bright and fiery, but it consumes my core with cold.

I have invoked the light in an attempt to burn away the rot inside me. Yet it persists, this flame. I am now its host. It is proof that this putrefaction has continued to fuel it.

By allowing my soul to fester, I have become light.

I am justice incarnate.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_17: I saw the sun today, buried beneath the soil. Screaming. We have mistaken the sky for heaven. But heaven is underground, screaming, waiting, eating its own. I will dig until I find its heart. And kill it.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_18: Fire cleanses what prayer cannot. The wings are gone. Torn from me by doubt. But the flame—pure and voiceless—remains. I set alight the chapel. Not out of spite. But mercy. Let them burn clean.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_19: The Queen sent me with a banner. I returned with an altar. My crusade is holy because it has no restraint. Let every sinner be ash. Let every shadow know my name. Azareth, flame of the final hymn.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_05_20: The beasts are broken men. The men are beasts with clean hands. There is no difference. But there will be order. Order through pain. Order through flame. I have begun sharpening the hymns into blades.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_01: They say she sleeps beneath the castle, but her shadow walks freely. It drifts down corridors like silk and slithers beneath doorways. Last week it passed me. It smelled like lavender and death.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_02: Something moved in the treeline, but left no tracks. The dogs wouldn’t follow. When I returned, my shadow was longer than it had been and it kept turning to face me when I wasn’t looking.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_03: The Upyr Queen of Carmilla is not visible by torchlight, but moonlight reveals her walking backward through the corridors. I watched her pass three guards unnoticed. Their shadows stayed behind, twitching.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_04: We lit lanterns at every window, but the shadow still came. It didn’t fall, it rose. Blacker than night, shaped like a man who remembers your name. It whispered mine from my father’s throat.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_05: The Queen never drank. She whispered. That's all. Whispers to the cook, the guards, the kings. Then no one else spoke anymore. Even now I hear her voice behind my teeth.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_06: Names carved in black ink. Some smudged beyond recognition. Others glowing faintly, as if recently spoken aloud. One name was circled in gold: Vayla. We burned the page. It returned.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_07: She speaks when the moon is fat with blood. Her tongue splits into seven. Her eyes glow. She says things only the dead should know. And they listen.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_08: The nobles pay handsomely for it. But I won’t drink it. Not after hearing Lady Venn scream ‘Mother?’ in her sleep for three nights running. She was an orphan.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_09: The 13th does not sleep. It hums when I write. I tried to dispel it, but it merely laughed—my laugh. It wears my face now. And it watches when I bathe.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_10: God was not present. We sang the hymn. Then we were ash and outline. Let this note be my penance.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_11: The well ran red for three days. We thought it was rust or algae. Then the livestock stopped drinking. Then the children started sleepwalking. They all went to the well. One climbed in. We never saw her again.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_12: DO NOT EAT THE DEER. Their blood is wrong. It burns. It sings. It sees you.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_13: They sang in harmony for hours. When I finally asked what the occasion was, they told me it wasn’t a song. It was a draining. The Countess likes to make her meals sing as she bleeds them.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_14: Each year the blood tithe increases. This spring, five carts of villagers were sent. The Queen said nothing, but afterward, roses grew in the hall. Their petals were veined and warm to the touch.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_15: He said, “If your nose bleeds at dusk, don’t wipe it. Don’t speak. Don’t move. She’ll take it as an invitation. Blood on the air is how she hunts. Just let it fall. Let it feed the dirt.”
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_16: A fountain that ran dry for years now flows again, but with blood, not water. No one dares dismantle it. They say it comes from within the stone. Sometimes, it pulses.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_17: We buried her with rites, sealed her coffin with iron nails and faith. But come morning, her blood was painted on the chapel walls, her own name written over and over. The coffin was empty. The nails still intact.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_18: They rule nothing but ash and sorrow. Yet none surrender. The wereraven cuts, the werewolf breaks, the ghost possesses our own. Every battle is a stalemate soaked in kin-blood.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_19: Do not eat. Do not sleep beneath the boughs. Do not believe what the fruit says. Especially when it uses your mother’s voice.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_06_20: One of them drank his own tongue. One grew wings. One cried for her mother. Three walked out alive, but only one cast a shadow. I saw it twist the floor.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_07_01: It's no wonder they call it the Rotten Apple. Nothing but bitter cold and even colder taxes by the King. They say the King is a ghost. But a ghost doesn't care about coins.\n\n"Wagon of wheat every week," they say. It's become a children's rhyme. It boils my blood, rotten core and all.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_07_02: I swear by all that is sacred. I braved the Wilds, and like the Goddess herself became reborn anew.\n\nThey say the Huntress still abides the rightful cycle of life and death. That she lives. By all that is sacred, I swear. After an eternity in this Nighthaven, I soon wonder if the Beast Cults of old will rise again. And return us to our rightful fury.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_07_03:
Heathens above and sinners below, the rightful Heir to Life is the claw, the fang, and the crooked tooth. Blood pays for blood. Gold cannot be traded.
Remember this.

Remember the Beast Lords.
Say their names: Taurus, Kurok, Mahantaram, Shirzad, Shah-Neshen, Uttu, Takhi, Fenrir, Ratatoskr, Huginn and Muninn, Winter Warrior, and Ursa.

Remember.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_07_04:
It's the darnedest thing. I went to harvest some apples today and what did I see but some shiny apples, yellower than the sun.

Sure are pretty, but what good is a gold apple? People want them shiny red apples, not whatever abomination this is.

There once was a girl who was born from a sunflower, on a late-summer morn. The stalk bent over as the bud opened up and the flower formed a bed for her on the tilled earth. An old farmer found her and named her Galbena Floare. Her hair was gold and her eyes were brown and she dressed all in shades of green.

She soon grew very tall, but Galbena Floare never spoke and only turned her face towards the sun on bright days and hung her head down when it rained, until one day, she stopped moving and could only stare eastward no matter the weather. The farmer tried to take care of Galbena, but she remained rooted in place until she withered away, leaving a thousand tiny black seeds where she had stood, and the farmer became very sad.

At harvest time, the farmer’s sunflower fields bloomed again, and each flower’s face followed the farmer instead of the sun.

Heed these words, Oh Children of Dunwood, for they may save your life!

There is that which waits to be perceived, so that it may enter your sphere. Should you look out your window at night, it may be waiting neath the sill. On the first night its back will be turned, and safe you will be, but on the following night, it will face your window, and should it espy that you perceive it, then you will have let it in. Beware, for on the third night, as you turn to blow out your candle, it will be there, in the darkest corner of your room. Do not look at its face, for if you meet its eyes, the invitation is made, and it will send you to the unseen world so it may take a place in your home.

So go to bed when your parents tell you, and pull the covers over your head, for if you do not see it, then it can not see you.

2. Do not linger in thresholds.
3. Do not sit in the northern corner of a room.

6. Should you hear your mother’s voice calling you, go back inside.

I met a cat in the crossroads, twas both betwixt and between. I looked in all directions, and nary a soul was seen.

The cat at me, he stared a while, then opened his mouth and said, “Goodsir, are you coming or going? Are you alive or dead?” I answered “Alive, I’ll be going,” and the cat cocked his head to the side; I followed his gaze behind me, and found that my body had died.

The cat at me, he grinned so wide, with rows of gleaming teeth. I said to the cat, how came you by, such fine points as these? The cat grinned wider and wider, his eyes locked straight on mine. He said “Goodsir, were they slighter, I’d not catch souls so fine.”

topic_17_nighthaven_body_08_07:
Once upon a time, when the world was young, and trees could talk, the Sun and the Moon were alive.

Now, the Sun desperately loved the Moon, but it could not move from its path. Its job was too important, and bringing light to the world had to come first.

Over time, this made the Moon very sad, doubting its own worth as work always came first for the Sun. They grew worried when the Sun did not visit them as much as they would like.

So the Moon asked the Sun, “Would you still love me, even if my face changed?”

And the Sun replied, “Yes. I will always love you no matter how you look.”

And the Moon asked, “Would you love me if I was a rabbit or a baboon or a deer?”

And the Sun replied, “Yes. I would love you even if you were an ibis or a serpent or an old man.”

The Moon smiled and shifted in it’s path. If the Sun could not move, perhaps the Moon could be more flexible.

Shadows played across its face. “Then if you cannot come to me, I shall visit you. And the world will just have to deal with you having some time off.”

The Sun replied, “I would like that.”

And so it came to be that eclipses came to the world, a few moments of darkness when the Sun and the Moon could forget about work for a short while.

Which is why we honor them and do no work during eclipses.

topic_17_nighthaven_body_08_10:
When the wolf first came, it came like winter, soft-footed, sharp-toothed, smelling of snow and hunger.
It lingered by the threshold for days, pacing, leaving paw prints in the frost that never seemed to melt. I watched it from the window, the way its yellow eyes caught the candlelight, the way it tilted its head when you laughed inside.

You never heard it scratching at the wood at night.
I told you it was nothing, just the wind in the eaves.

But one evening, while you slept, I opened the door.
I thought: Better it come in on my terms than on its own.
It padded across the floor, so large it seemed to dim the room. I offered it bread and meat, but it took only my hand in its jaws, gently, like a lover leading me somewhere I did not want to go but could not resist.

It lay down at the foot of our bed that night, tail curled like a scythe. You breathed easier, no longer tossing from dreams. I told myself I had done right.

Weeks passed. The wolf learned your scent. It learned your name. It learned how to mimic the weight of my hand on your back when you slept, the warmth of my voice in the morning. Slowly, it crept closer, not to me, but to you.

And then one night, I woke to find it beside you, not at my feet.
Its fur brushed your bare skin.
Its teeth showed when it smiled in the dark.
You murmured something and curled into it, as though you had always known it, as though it had been me all along.

Now, the wolf sleeps in our bed.
I lie awake in the cold space it has left me, listening to you breathe against its chest. It wears your smile now, and sometimes, when you speak to it, I am not sure if you remember I was ever here at all.

But I keep the door open.
Somehow, I think that is what it wanted.

From the black marshes beyond God’s map came the Hexen Sisters—Isolde, Mirabel, and Elfrun—born not of womb but of smoke, moonlight, and dying men’s sighs. No priest dares call them holy, yet their beauty undoes prayer.

Isolde smiles like a sickle and steals hearts with a kiss upon the palm. Mirabel sings until bones slip from their joints, her victims dancing gladly as marrow drains. Elfrun, fairest and cruelest, embraces like an angel fallen—her thighs a grave yielding no escape.

Men seek them, though none return whole. Some wander home smiling, lips blue and eyes glass. Others stumble the roads muttering in tongues of ash, their strength spent upon the Sisters’ altar of flesh.

Once, a hunter clad in silver and oak swore to end them. Thrice he struck, thrice they rose, laughing, naked in flame and shadow. At dawn his heart was nailed to his door, his body gone, a crimson trail leading back to the marsh.

So the old wives warn: if thou hearest laughter sweet as wine at the wood’s edge, flee. The Hexen do not hunger for bread, nor blood alone—but for the surrender of will itself. To love them once is forever.

Electricity remains the only force I have found that both offends and fascinates the supernatural. A spark against a ghoul’s flesh sends it into spasm, neither pain nor pleasure, but something older, a memory of the Sun that once scoured their kind. Upyr recoil as though struck by a priest’s relic, though no holy blessing hums within the coil. Curiously, ghosts behave in the opposite fashion: they drink the charge, their forms sharpening, eyes brightening with a hunger they cannot name. Werewolves are unpredictable—some snarl and lunge through the shock, their blood singing, while others collapse into a shivering, whimpering heap.

The most troubling discovery came tonight with the wraith I tethered in the copper cage. I passed a steady current through the bars, and it began to speak. Not words, but shapes in the air—images of burning cities, red oceans, and a sky torn open to something… watching. When I cut the current, the visions ceased, and the wraith wailed like a newborn abandoned. I am left to wonder: is electricity not a bane or a boon to these creatures, but a language? If so, who taught it to them—and are they trying to teach it to me?

Tomorrow, I will increase the voltage. I must know what the next message says.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_11:
Legends, folklore, campfire tales, and childrens' bedtime stories suggest that Upyr drain memories and thoughts, but I cannot be called a scientist and that's an unproven theory (but highly suggested everywhere it seems).

Descriptions state an Upyr begins with raising of arms, the victim floating in the air, tendrils of blue energy snaking from the eyes and mouth of the victim to the mouth of the host. At least that's how I remember it.

Upyr drainings, while seemingly rare, are quite common they say. I have indeed heard this to be true. Nonetheless:

Physical symptoms might be sunken eyes, listless expressions, dizziness and confusion, lethargy, sleeplessness, paranoid delusions, lucid dreams, vivid nightmares, loose stools, waking hallucinations both auditory and visual which grip the mind and resolve in no further conflict than the undoubted existential truth that we live in a precoded simulacrum of reality stored on electricity, strange new addictions, and very very very rarely, a slight headache.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_12: Far to the northwest there lies an untamed, untapped, and elden region that folks have been suggesting is an undiscovered civilization on Aeternum. Surely this land has a multitude of secrets, yet surprise often finds those who doubt the creativity and ingenuity of mankind over eons.\n\nIn this report, I, Claudius Maxwell duBois, will unravel the unknowable, usurp the usual, journey *into the west*, and paint a picture of Mantravan - The Jungle of Sound.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_13:
Research indicates that many pre-history Aeternians still survive in the corners of this island. One such interview occurred at the Rose Red. I spoke with a non-descript, unidentifiable person of repute to which I will factually and scientifically verify the following claims:

I. The person of repute claims a vast tropical jungle filled with pre-historic Ancient ruins and perhaps the original Capital City of the Ancients exists somewhere on the border of Nighthaven to the northwest.

II. The person of repute also claims that a species of Ancient Guardian still survives to this day in this land - albeit not as a bag of sentient, violent bones. But real people, monks even! They've maintained their spirituality and connection to the infinite. And they practice singing, dancing, and yoga to achieve enlightenment! Sounds like heaven. (Note to Reader: Do you understand my pun?)

III. The person of repute, at last, claims that this Ancient civilization used Sound as a major mechanical energy source. Vibrations, signals, and waves of all mathematical varieties can be heard, echoed, and even sometimes seen with the naked eye. A phenomena that intrigues me the most.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_14:
My journey to Mantravan began one fateful day, when I sought passage on an unmarked vessel bound for riches and treasure. A pirate captain with a fiery attitude and even fierier hair led the voyage.

We skipped the rocky outcrops surrounding Pentacle Rock, journeyed along the coast until we ran aground on great towers of stone dredged from the deep. The passage here is definitely impassable, by boat, or carriage.

Still, the journey was sufficiently well worth it.

Night was falling, and we had come to journey's end.
I asked the crew, "What can you see on the horizon?"
A voice shot back from the crow's nest, "A light on the water!"
"No, all is turning to silver glass!"
Before I could respond, the voice commanded, "Across the sea, a pale moon rises!"

As we anchored for the evening off the coast of a great jungled biome, multiple sailors and henchmen aboard the vessel reported hearings of soft, still, and peaceful chants. Hymns echoing off the rocks. Gentle harps, and what sounded like an angelic choir lulled us all to sleep.
'May it be?' I thought to myself. 'Mantravan is real.'

Safe in the arms of the choir, only sleeping, we dreamed of the ones who came before.

But it was no siren-song. We awoke refreshed, replenished. One sailor even claims her eyesight had improved.

We unmoored and returned home. I still dream about the sounds of the singing monks to this day. I remember the white gulls calling, and ask myself, why were they so quiet and so loud, that I could hear the chants and songs clear as day midst noise and chaos?

It was as if a dream out of memory and time. I won't say we have come now to the end.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_15:
It is my duty, and my privilege, to announce my retirement from Aeternian geography and history. I have heard the sounds and waves of a higher calling into the west. I will set sail on a rowboat armed with nothing but an oar and a dream. I leave my journal here with you, so that one day you too may journey on grey ships’ sails to Mantravan and find me again. I leave my collegiate cartographer's ring as a symbol of my newfound purpose. I shall go now.

And once arrived, I will lay down my sweet and weary head.
White shores are calling.

You and I will meet again.

Claudius Maxwell duBois, Retired Cartographer
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_16: Dunwood is alight with Ipomoea spp, illuminating my path after dusk falls. A unique species of this Ipomoea spp. refracts the moonlight in such a way that it creates a spectrum of color visible under my microscope. This small, fulgent flower shall be referred to furthermore as Ipomoea prismatica. I would like to see if this opalescent flower could withstand the dyeing process and what textiles it could bind to to retain its prismatic appearance.\n
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_17: With assistance from my young apprentice Archibald, we have gathered enough specimens of Ipomoea prismatica to study its uses. While I explore its medicinal uses, for some local claims of use appear to be unfounded, I have tasked Archibald with trialing different ways to extract the essence of the petals to be used as a dye. He claims his first attempts suggested the mordant lacked a strong enough coordination complex to hold I. prismatica’s full spectrum of color, leading to a monochromatic result. Alternate theories suggest that the color is not produced by the spirit of the plant itself, but perhaps the combination of it and the surrounding light. Further inspection of the specimen is required.\n
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_18: Sorrowthorn spreads like a plague upon the land, infecting trees within the Dunwood. Biodiversity is limited in areas where S. exsanguis occupies. Sorrowthorn creates an expansive rhizomal system underground, which combined with outcompeting other species within the forest by creating an impenetrable thicket, drains the life out of the surrounding landscape. It clings to the trees, almost in a parasitic manner. S. exsanguis digs into the environment, jaundiced both in appearance and behavior.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_09_19:
Ob. locals suffering from a malady of madness. Those heavily affected are prone to wane faces appearing pallid and bloodless.

Dorian Tea

Spagyrism can be used with wildcrafted Spina exsanguis to create a tea. This tea, when taken early and regularly if infected, can help stave off maladies of the mind. With the madness at bay, those suffering from the withering mind may maintain their youthful appearance.

Note: This tisane can carry a high astringency due to the high tannin content. To reduce astringency, add a generous amount of honey.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_01:
What is death on an island where nothing can die? Where the very trees come back after being chopped down.

Is this what it means to face transformative change? Or are we stagnant because we are coming back as we were, with no true death to propel us to exceed?

What is life without the threat of death?

I will need to ponder more on this.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_02:
Have you thought about your toes? Like, really thought about them?

How the big toe is required for perfect balance? How the pinky toe is so small. How some people can pick things up their their toes?

Sometimes that's all I think about…
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_03: I remember a time when I was young, and free, and alive. Now the gray twisted spider web of my memory stretches, pulls, until it breaks like dried yarn in a sunblasted barn. Where was the vitality? Where was the energy? Why do I want to write a thousand words to describe my pain but I only understand that fifty of them will be read by human eyes?
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_04: Most folks fear death ‘cause they think it’s an ending. Me? I’ve dug enough holes to know it’s more like a door. You never see what’s behind it ‘til you’re shoved through… but I’ve heard the knocking from the other side, and they sound eager.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_05: Light’s not good by itself, too much of it blinds. Darkness isn’t bad either, too much of it hides the snakes, but also the roses. A lantern’s worth is in the flicker between them… the space where your eyes start lying to you.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_06: The sea takes what it wants and leaves the rest to rot. Fish, men, even memories. I used to pray for calmer waters, but now I pray for teeth sharp enough to bite back.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_07: Every shape hides inside something else. A face in a skull. A lie in the truth. People think I carve bones into charms. But no, I carve charms until they turn into bones again.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_08: Nobody wears a mask to hide who they are. They wear it to show who they wish they could be, without the risk of dying for it. Trouble is, keep it on long enough and it stops coming off.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_09: Patient relayed same intentional and codified phrase, likely stemmed from recently-published and discovered combined vocal and multiple motor tic disorder I do believe this is the first time something like this has been recorded. Patient repeatedly repeats verbal phrase as following was recorded during initial medical check, and I quote:\n\n"Death. Death. Death. [ad infinitum]“
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_10:
Patient polititely excused self to lavatory, returned, and fell asleep. After several minutes of reassurance, Patient devolved from regular persona into new, undetermined side-personality, also known as Split Personality, and in recent circles, Pluralism. Subject attended by nursing and doctorate staff until presumed safe. Patient then was recorded during initial medical check, and I quote, whispered under breath:

"Kill. Kill. Kill. [ad infinitum]"

Subject was given sedative solution and warm goatmilk, put to bed.

Current thoughts suggest that Patient likely resorts to childhood-based coping mechanisms, proffered by severe emotional, verbal, and I would guess physical abuse during adolescence.

Patient resorts to intrusive thought-making, intentionally addictive coping behaviors, and highly dysregulated emotional resonance.

Physician's scientific recommendation: yet another of God's failed creatures; recommendations include leeches, bloodletting, cleansing of Humors, and trepanning.

Case closed.
Physican Thompson
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_11: Lykania posited the paradox that should Asena have a den, The Den of Asena, and over time each part of the den were replaced with new wood, new dirt, new rocks, and new roots, until there was no part of the original burrow left, would it still be the same Den of Asena?
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_12: Berskir raised that if an Upyr were placed inside a giant baguette with both mustard and honey and relish, then the Upyr would be simultaneously alive and undead until devoured, and that the Upyr would also be a sandwich.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_13: Lenore quoth that the realism of air as the element by which corvids fly must be true if taking an epistemological approach to the nature of reality. Though wind cannot be seen, it has measurable effects on its environment, including but not limited to audible whispers, and howls, and bringing with it certain humours when blowing from different directions. Under the laws of abductive heuristics, the hypothesis of the reality of air wins out as that which makes the fewest assumptions.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_14: Dear Diary, Today the Town Stylemancer called me, The Lady Lucrezza, a Hedonist?! Why, I don’t even know the meaning of the word! But it was leveled as an insult, make no mistake. As if disposing of my modiste each season were of some offence? They said I am trying to fill a void, a hole where my soul used to be. The nerve! Am I to wear outdated fashion made by tired minds? Is trendsetting in high fashion not my sole source of euphoria amidst the dull machinations of society? And besides, there is always a new supply of dressmakers who are happy to volunteer after the last one disappears. It is too glamorous a position to turn down.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_15: The nobility of Nighthaven maintain elaborate Houses of the Dead, if you could even call them ‘dead’. Yet we, the Living of Nighthaven, the beating heart of this land, are bled dry until we succumb to the passage of time. Why should the dead have higher quality of life than the living? Catacombs, lichyards, tombs, and mausoleums outnumber townships and farms; their upkeep saps valuable resources that could instead be used to improve our own homes. We demand ethical reform, prioritize the living over the dead! Let us seize the means of construction!
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_16:
8:31 AM
"Now I am really, completely awake for the first time."
8:37 AM
"This time I am awake. I am conscious. I have never been awake before."
8:45 AM
"Now I am perfectly, absolutely awake. It’s the first time ever."
[Previous entries crossed out]
9:02 AM
"I am finally awake, this is the first time. All others were dreams."
9:07 AM
"Diana just left. I miss her already. When did she go?"
9:12 AM
"Just now I became conscious. I feel a great clarity, as if I have just woken for the first time. I must write it down. This is the first real moment of awareness."

[Notes in the margins, written later:] "Everything before now is a blank. I am seeing the world for the first time. It’s as if I’ve never lived until now."

[The diary continues in this way for the rest of the entries.]
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_17:
A thousand sleepless nights, for what, yet left wanting? Why am I heretofore unto known of all sin preclaimed? My madness is infectuous beyond resin or reason. I am a doubtful liar, of unaccustomed trepanning. Couldst thou dare trifle with Wit's Witless End? Nay, good morrow, to you and on the seventeenth of April, I shan't tarry a moment sooner too.

GOOD DAY AND GOOD NIGHT HAVEN!

[The letter appears to be sealed with a kiss.]
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_18: I wait and I wait and nothing happens. I cry and I cry and nothing changes. Nobody hears me. Nobody sees me. I am alone. I am alone. There is no hope. All is lost. Forgiveness is not a sin.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_19: I hate it all. I hate it all. I am so terrified all the time. Anxiety crushes me like the weight of a boulder, constant crushing pain. So much pain. I cannot breathe. And then I panic, and then I scream. And I then scare everyone and everything. It begins as my fault. It ends as my fault. I am always at fault. I am cursed. I am a walking corpse. There is no hope.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_10_20: My pain is not important. My worries are not valid. I am a crushing seething pulsing barb of agony. I am not whole. I am lambasted under the weight of a titanic-sized concern. Just a concern. A small worry. That inevitably consumes my every living thought and action. Am I sane? Am I present? Is this real? What is real? Help me. Anyone. Please. Help me. This is a cry for help. I am so lost midst all the seas of terror in my mind like a drifting buoy lost in darkness. There is no god.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_01:
I have done everything there is to do in Nighthaven and now I find myself with an abundance of time with nothing more to do.

I shall hold a party outdoors. I shall have my thralls bring every piece of furniture outside and we shall feast underneath the stars, enjoying the evening air.

Who shall I invite? It must be everyone of importance. I shall start with my neighbors to the north. I'm sure they would love a chance to sup outdoors.

Except the evening air is rather chilly this time of year. And there are all those animals that might try to stop by. Terribly unclean, animals.

Hmm, perhaps I shall hold this on the roof instead. I believe we have some sort of gallery up there. Yes, I shall get my thralls to carry all this furniture back inside and up to the rooftop gardens. It shall be perfect.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_02:
I am so terribly bored. I decided to have my thralls rearrange every painting in this place by the amount of red paint used.

I have given them three days to complete this task. They are to start in the main library, then the ballroom, then the sitting room, the other sitting room, the guest sitting room, and finally end with the corridors.

I have forgotten how many paintings I've collected over time. Perhaps I should have them do the bedrooms too? Or the great hall?

It been so long I don't even remember how many rooms this place has. Perhaps I will go for a walk to jog my memory.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_03:
The clocks count time endlessly here.

If you stand close enough you can hear each second tick away. Each moment encapsulated in a single sound.

Tick. Tock.

And do not get me started on the clocktower. You cannot go far enough away from hearing that ring. I know, I tried. But somehow it always calls me back.

I have asked my Thralls to remove all the clocks from this place. I already know what time it is.

It's the time for eternal boredom.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_04:
Lord Bathory invited me to an utterly boring party tonight. Truly, it was the most passe thing I have had the displeasure of attending in a long time. 

The food looked wilted. The people were terrified, which is just what you would expect with Bathory.

Really, the entire dinner party and promised spectacle were nothing new, just the same old scene of terror we’ve all been served before.

Truly, being this bored is exhausting. I think I’ll head home early.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_05:
Books, books, books. So many books. Our bookcases are overflowing. Absolutely filled with books. And I’ve read them all.

I’ve read them so many times I have the titles memorized. The Inferior Man, The Stone Skull Charter, The Book of Shadows, The Cannonomicon, The Siren Queen's Proclamations. I've read, studied, translated, and mastered the Ancient Glyphs. I've placed my hand and communed with the Signets of the Beast Lords. I have even studied and recorded the many lessons of the Arcana Cards. I have even read and transcribed the literal inscriptions of the Monuments of Brimstone, the Glory of the Republic, the Great Pyramid of Akhet, the Great Wall of Nebet-Het, and even the hidden and heretofore unknown record of Diana's Nemorensis.

So many, and yet they did not fill the time as promised. I am so tired with them all.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_06:
Look at these arches. The windows, such exacting detail in every pane of glass, all to tell a story no one will see because no one looks up.

Simply being around such beauty and recognizing it day after day is exhausting. I will need a nap after this, but alas, I cannot sleep.

Perhaps I should move to a simple shack in the woods. But then I would notice each imperfection of the grain on the walls. No, far better to be here, surrounded by beauty, even if it is overwhelming.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_07:
Traveling is so abominably slow. Why can I not just go immediately to where I need to be?

Why must I get a thrall to get my carriages ready, and then head out only once they say everything is finally able to go?

And these thralls! They are so slow at packing, at getting the carriages situated. It’s not my fault I need to have twenty suitcases with me. I need to bring my own dishes, just in case there is poison!

But truly, sitting in a carriage, watching the landscape change, how utterly boring.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_08:
Food doesn’t bring the joy it once did. All flavors are just one flavor now, an endless banquet of dust, with the texture of sawdust, desiccated and dry.

It is like there is a desert where overripe fields used to be. The heady aromas that were linked to each season, the rich wines, and richer sauces. All just memories now, as I consume pale imitations.

Why do I keep trying? This is futile. I should just leave, but I continue to hope that someday, the flavor will return.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_09:
I do not need to sleep anymore. Resting is something that other people do, not me. My keen intellect keeps me sharp and poised for action at all times.

I find that watching people who do need sleep leaves a lot to be desired. Why, they react most angrily to being poked awake when you wish for them to respond to some clever point you have made.

I need conversation, daresay I thrive on it, and I cannot surround myself with weak sleepers. No, I must seek out other intellectuals who also need not sleep.

I believe I shall have my thrall fetch my carriage. It is time we went visiting.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_11_10:
It’s so tedious to keep a journal, writing in it, day after day, sentence after sentence, word after word.

What a chore to pour out such thoughts across paper, making sure the ink doesn’t stain the voluminous lace at my cuffs.

If I didn’t write, why I would be spared this boredom. I could occupy my time with more pressing matters. Like what dried flowers to arrange into vases in the entryway.

But even that grows tiresome. Truly, there is nothing to do in this land of time eternal.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_12_01:
First he has us carry all the furniture outside, those heavy rugs and everything!

All for some evening concert he hadn't even sent invitations out for.

Three hours later he changes his mind and has us carry everything back inside, up multiple flights of stairs to hold an outdoor evening on the roof.

I don't think he even knows how to get up to the roof.

We just left the furniturn in the stairs and started up a card game, since he'll forget he asked us to do this in another hour or two, and we're not moving it again.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_12_02: Jokes on my master, I can't see the color red. So I've taken to organizing the paintings based on how many weapons are in them. I figure, the more weapons, the redder, right?\n\nWell, he's going to forget he ordered me to do this in about two hours, so I just have to pretend I'm doing this work until then.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_12_03: Got my hands on a new Arcana deck. If anyone wants to play, we'll be in the basement around midnight, pretending to clean out the spare storeroom. Remember to bring something to ante in, if you are interested.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_12_04:
We’re going on a light journey, he says. Just enough clothes for the weekend, he says. I’m sure they have their own thralls to help with the carrying, he says.

Here I am, lugging six, SIX, carriages worth of ruffles and lace outfits up twenty flights of stairs for this weekend’s ball. The other thralls were all busy with other ridiculous tasks set upon them by the other Upyr here. I’ll be lucky if I’m done before tomorrow getting these all aired and into the wardrobe.

Is this my life now? I expected a bit more when I became an Upyr.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_12_05:
That’s it. I’m done. I’m going to find another master to work for. There has to be an opening in House Carmilla, or one of the many minor houses.

I’m not going to put up with this treatment any more. We’re not like those ancient skeletons you see in the ruins, going through the motions like some automaton. We have feelings. And right now my feeling is that no one should have to endure this sort of abuse.

Goodbye. I won't even wish you good luck at finding a replacement.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_01: The walls sweat venom here. I collected three vials before the dripping began to match the rhythm of my heartbeat. Something above me… no—beneath the skin of the stone—watched. I wrapped my leg in silk to slow the poison. It whispered when I touched it.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_02: Marked my passage with chalk. Then web. Then bones. Then nothing. There’s a softness to the dark here. It's like the cave itself breathes through its many mouths. I found the queen’s chamber. I think. She’s still growing. So many eyes.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_03: The gold was strung in silk, every coin hung like bait. I should’ve known. They left it for me. I took one. Only one. Now my boots are stitched to the floor and I can’t blink without tasting thread.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_04: No treasure here—only eggs. Hundreds. Maybe thousands. Each as large as a fist and pulsing with warmth. I saw my own reflection in the silk, but older, and smiling. Something just touched my shoulder and my sword arm won’t move.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_05: Set the traps. Left the bait. Came back to find the traps woven shut, lined with my own hair. The crag sings when the wind cuts right. Sounds like clicking. Sounds like legs.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_06: This is Ésagila, once the seat of kings. Now a nest of secrets and spinners. Every throne webbed, every book blank or written in silk. I glimpsed Uttu from afar. She was graceful, divine, awful. She hummed, and I felt my blood trying to crawl out of me.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_07: Map says this hall leads to the old vaults. It doesn’t. It leads in a circle, but the walls shift ever so slightly. Every turn leaves new silk on my boots. And the air smells like rotting honey. Something is guiding me. Watching. I haven’t seen my shadow in hours.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_08: I stepped on one of the eggs. Thought it was a stone. It burst. Screaming things poured out, and I fell into a pit of them. So soft, like falling into warm fur. They didn’t bite. They burrowed. My hands feel strange now.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_09: O Light that guides, deliver me from this cursed hollow. The web clings to my armor like rot. My sword sticks in its sheath. I heard the name Uttu whispered from the throat of a man long dead. His mouth was sewn shut. I am not alone.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_10: The trap wasn't meant to kill. It just held me long enough to see my past in silk. My mother’s face, then my own, then something with too many eyes. It’s not a web. It’s a siphon for my memories. I forgot my name yesterday. Today, I forgot my mission.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_13_11: Crossed the bridge. Almost made it. Then I saw it. Galrot. Legs like tree trunks, body like a fortress of bone and black glass. It didn’t chase. Just stood there, clicking its fangs, waiting. Like it knew I’d have to turn back. Like it always knows.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_14_01: Cronewell Cathedral, though crumbling, is a perfect example of the architectural style of Nighthaven’s second age. Structures in this style incorporate traits of both Romanesque and Gothic Architecture, combining heavy masonry with pointed arches. It is a more humble structure than others in its class, lacking the elaborate tracery, rose windows, and crockets that Tularest Abbey so resplendently displays, and lacking the flying buttresses of Castle Dracula and House Carmilla nearby.\n\nCronewell is notable for its twin windows on the south end of the nave, where the lower sills mirror the lancets typically only seen along upper lintels. The two statues in niches at the outer vestibule are examples of the “Veiled Figures” motif that is favored throughout Nighthaven for cloth exquisitely carved from stone. Strangely, the cathedral’s narthex is a portcullised gatehouse, as if, rather than welcome the pious in, the builders sought to keep something out.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_14_02:
Finally, I have seen the Athenaeum of the Sage King! How grand it is. Having already toured the Buru of Irkalla and the old House Dracul, I can safely say that the North and South halls are contemporary, and pre-date House Dracul by centuries, if not millenia.

The Athenaeum of the Sage King is a sprawling complex, not unlike those that dot the other territories of Aeternum, save for the prevailing feature of circular patterns adorning the site, a trait indicative of the southern and western modes. A frieze along the northern exterior wall depicts three ancient “Figures of Power,” though their identities are a source of contention. The main structure, similar to a stupa, is a monolithic dome, carved from a single stone in the intensely laborious rock-cut style. The dome’s interior features a great oculus, in which a golden orb is still magnificently set.

The entire site is reminiscent of beautiful Raktapura back home, and leads one to wonder, could these halls have been used for coronation ceremonies?
topic_17_nighthaven_body_14_03: Algarot Hall. According to records, this place was formidable to behold in its time. Alas, in this age, it is diminished to scattered remains of skeletal stonework. The great arches shouldering Algarot’s North and South wings are still worth the trip for those with an interest in three-tiered arcuated construction, funicular curves, and counterbalanced spandrels.\n\nThe hall has been home to numerous high ranking Inquisition members, but most famously belonged to Decimus Constantus Gabrielli-Gorgette, the Mad Archdeacon of Algarot, and his Diaconate of the Undying Light. Interestingly, Algarot Hall appears to have broken ground shortly after the completion of House Dracul, as both buildings are of relatively the same age and style. Perhaps there is some correlation to their near-simultaneous emergence…
topic_17_nighthaven_body_14_04:
Ah the Towers of Nighthaven, you’ve seen one, you’ve seen them all, as they say. Well I have seen them all, and personally find it fascinating that each tower is an almost exact copy of the next. Considering their number and distance apart, this seems an impressive feat of engineering. Perhaps an exchange of ideas amongst builders is likely? Or are there more mystical underpinnings to the duplication of these soaring edifices?

The Tower of the Emperor has the same Romano-Gothic style as the numerous chapels and halls across Nighthaven. This style is much older than the Baroque and Late Gothic manors and castles that many Upyr Families now favor. Infact, I have seen the undercroft of Castle Dracula and believe it is of this same period, indicating the castle has seen several eras of construction, each layering a new style on top of the old.

Thick walls bastion the tower, and the few windows give an almost fortress-like appearance, but to what purpose? Rough rib vaults along the interior passages allow for high ceilings over the endlessly spiraling staircases leading to the upper keep. Meanwhile, a collection of Grotesques loom over the eaves and corbels, guarding the magically sealed doorways.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_01:
Paragraph 55
The Warrior King comes across a marvelous room filled with piles of many treasures. The moment he steps forward into the room, there is the telltale click of a trap. With only a moment to think, what direction does he move?

To move forward and to the right, turn to paragraph 89.
To move backwards and to the left, turn to paragraph 196.

Paragraph 56
After burning the mushrooms, a doorway is revealed leading to another room. Massive tree roots have pierced the ceiling and grown down inside this room, allowing a single shaft of light to enter and illuminate a chest upon a pedestal. There is water all around the pedestal, and a series of crates stacked along the wall.

To swim to the pedestal, turn to paragraph 103.
To climb up the crates, turn to paragraph 134.

Paragraph 57
The closest shortcut shown on the map seems safe enough. A lever opens a narrow corridor just large enough to slip inside. No sooner does the Warrior King step inside, the hidden door closes, and there is no lever on this side. Determined to go forward, the Warrior King starts down the corridor, only to have slicing blades whirl out of the walls, while larger blades drop down from above.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_02:
Paragraph 88
The scroll is not as delicate as it seems, it proves to be the Sage King’s map of these ancient halls. There are notations of shortcuts through various sections, which the Warrior King had not noticed when he previously went through them. There is also a room marked with an X near the center of the map.

To use the short cut from the map, turn to paragraph 57.
To use the map to get to the room with the X, turn to paragraph 104.

Paragraph 89
The Usurper anticipated this action, and a series of stone blocks crash down from the ceiling, exactly in front of the Warrior King. The Warrior King dodges the first three stones, but then a flame trap roars to life across the floor. While distracted by the pain from the burns, the Keystone comes crashing down, crushing the Warrior King's dreams of rule.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.

Paragraph 90
The Warrior King enters the impressive Sage King’s Archive and looks through the shelves. After examining all it has to offer, he plucks the Scroll of Forgotten Lore from where it rests. Now he shall learn the truth behind everything.
The Warrior King returns home, triumphant, certain he will rule forever. But, for the rest of his life he is haunted by images of what he could have gained, had he continued to search those Ancient Halls.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_03:
Paragraph 102
The Warrior King should have expected what happens next. The room shivers with scintillating colors. Everything smells wonderful, like a banquet fit for a king. After the Warrior King stuffs his face with mushrooms, the lethargy sets in. Muscles become numb. Falling facedown into the mushrooms, the spores fill his nostrils and the world goes quiet.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.

Paragraph 103
After reaching the pedestal, the Warrior King uses a jump pad to get up to it, opening the chest. Inside there are two items. A crumbling scroll that has seen better centuries, and a dark iron key that seems to slide away from his eyes.

To take the scroll, turn to paragraph 88.
To take the key, turn to paragraph 142.

Paragraph 104
The room is filled with crystals. They are not growing, as the Warrior King half expected, but are inlaid in the walls in meticulous patterns, dazzling the eyes as light strikes them from various braziers lit around the room. There are six braziers in total, three are lit, three are not.

To light all the braziers, turn to paragraph 141.
To plunge the room into darkness, turn to paragraph 198.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_04:
Paragraph 133
The storehouse is certainly unimpressive from the outside, but the interior more than makes up for it. Lavish tapestries adorn the walls. Bookshelves overflowing with rare tomes cover the few sections that don’t have tapestries. Plush chairs perfect to reading are strategically placed around the room. One bookshelf on the back wall is askew and there is a tapestry that blows from an unknown breeze.
To move the bookshelf to see what lies behind, turn to paragraph 90.
To investigate the tapestry, turn to… sadly the paragraph number has been smudged out and is illegible.

Paragraph 134
The crates lead up to a gallery and a path into another room. From there it is easy to bypass the rest of the traps and travel unimpeded to an ancient Throne Room deep within the ruins. It is there a might Scepter of Power is placed, just waiting for a true king to take it up once more.
The Warrior King returns home, triumphant, certain he will rule forever. But, for the rest of his life he is haunted by images of what he could have gained, had he continued to search those Ancient Halls.

Paragraph 135
The door opens into a cavern filled with water. The Warrior King steps in, for he can swim. After reaching a log he planned on using the climb out, the Warrior King realizes he’s made a terrible mistake. It is no log, but a very hungry crocodile. Who has been waiting so patiently for a snack. There isn’t even time to draw his sword.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_05:
Paragraph 141
With all the braziers lit, the crystals in the room are too much for the Warrior King’s eyes to take. Blinking and blinded, the Warrior King does not notice an Ancient Amalgam has awakened, clacking into the room, and crushing everything in its path, as it goes to turn off the braziers.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.

Paragraph 142
The Iron Key is heavy with the weight of ages upon it. Nothing in this room fits a key of this size, but the Warrior King remembers seeing two gates previously where it might go. One is ornate, covered with imposing iron spikes and entire hunting scenes wrought in textured sheets and twisted bars. The other is a simple gate, as one might have before a storehouse to keep supplies locked up tight.

To try the storehouse gate, turn to paragraph 133.
To try the ornate gate, turn to paragraph 197.
Paragraph 143
This room is filled with mushrooms of all varieties. Some glow. Some pulse. Some burst underfoot releasing a cloud of spores. Some release a bloody sap when touched. They cluster on walls, coat the floor, and ooze out of the ceiling.

To burn the mushrooms, turn to paragraph 56.
To eat the mushrooms, turn to paragraph 102.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_15_06:
Paragraph 196
The Usurper never expected anyone to move back, assuming thieves would be so focused on the treasure they would only move forward.

With the first trap out of the way, the path across the room is easily picked out from what stones do not have scorch marks. The treasure turns out to be nothing more than poorly gilded tin coins, utterly worthless. Hidden behind the piles of false treasure, are two doors.

To open the northeast door, turn to paragraph 135.
To open the northwest door, turn to paragraph 143.

Paragraph 197
The ornate gate is truly a work of art, and inserting the key within the lock lets out a wretched groan the likes of which would raise the dead. Which is exactly what it does. Wraiths pour out of the gate in fury at being awoken from their endless slumber. Or perhaps they were just angry at being locked inside and now can pass beyond the gate. Either way, the Warrior King is taken by surprise from the undead onslaught.
The Warrior King dies unfulfilled.

Paragraph 198
With the room dark, it is easy to spot the outline of a hidden door embedded in the right wall. Opening the door leads to a simple room, with a rough work desk covered in sketches and notes. This is what the Warrior King has been seeking. The plans he was certain the Sage King and the Usurper were working on together, behind his back.

By taking these he can sow confusion between them. Over time, if he plays his cards right, they will fall into distrust of each other. And then, he shall offer his help to each to bring the other down. So that only he, the Warrior King remains.

The Warrior King returns home, triumphant, certain he will rule forever, alone.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_02:
An eye that hears color, an ear that sees sound, and knows,
The eldest must meet the youngest before the inner gates,
Whom now the rolling plains of Chronos cover in wounds,
The breath and the embrace form the key to the ladder of the heavens.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_03:
Alone on an island, the lighted globe dies in silence,
Laid in the tomb of heroes, face turned to the sunset;
If silver spear speaks to silver spear of the wish and the wall,
You may conquer the world on a wave of pointing hands.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_04:
The owl follows its flight, despite the dogs frothing below,
The king seats himself amidships, both the pilot and pelorus, and
Unabandoned, grasps the helm fast while a crown of stars is worn;
The citadel is filled with allies, but another will navigate if he does not.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_05: You will observe many things from high places.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_06: A falling object will bring difficulty to your day.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_07: The wind turns its back to you today. The road will twist beneath your feet, coins will roll from your grasp, and friendly smiles may hide teeth. Walk slowly, speak little, and do not chase what slips away.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_08:
In this three card reading you start with the Hermit. In the past you lived alone, surrounded by books, doling out wisdom to the rare few who could find you.

The next card is the Five of Pentacles, a great loss befell you, everything is gone, ripped from you from actions outside your control. Your isolation became your protection.

Your final card is Judgement. A reckoning is upon you, and you shall reap what you have sown.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_09:
In this three card reading you start with the Moon. You have been betrayed by a close friend. This has colored all your friendships since then.

The next card is the Eight of Swords, and it comes as no surprise that you are grieving that loss of friendship. It's hard to make good decisions when the hurts of the past weigh down upon you.

Your final card is Rebirth. Do not worry, change is coming, and once you are transformed, you will be stronger for it.
topic_17_nighthaven_body_16_10:
In this three card reading you start with the Sun reversed. You have tasted joy, but it has been snatched away from you, and you are bitter about losing what you had.

The next card is the High Priestess. You see yourself as the bearer of Ancient knowledge, that which must be hidden from the rest of the world.

Your final card is the Tower. This does not stand for a place, but a warning. The house of cards you have built for yourself will come tumbling down, and there is nothing you can do to stop it, if you continue on your current path.
